baseShaSubject: Re-open four repair grants under amendment A2
grantsNothing: This return repairs four packets' participant instructions. It promotes no family, opens no commercial route, grants no approval, changes no live RCAP route, and is not a verification of its own work. All four families are released and await a fresh independent read.

standardApplied.a1Ordering: Ask FIRST whether the repository establishes the answer. If it does, the packet states it. Only where no held source establishes it may a NAMED checkable authority stand in.
standardApplied.a2Scope: The repository means every committed record the family binds PLUS every record the route obligation census names as a requiredSourceId for that route — the compiled state profile, the committed track registry, and the committed packet-set manifest including its participantActionRequired entries.
standardApplied.a2ConfirmedIndependentlyHere: A2 was not taken on trust. For each of the four families this worker located the route obligation census row itself, read its requiredSourceIds, opened the named record, and read the fee/service/filing text out of the committed bytes before writing a word. A2 is correct on all four; no family contradicted it.

claimDiscipline.serialised: Every claim.mjs call was run one family at a time, never in parallel, because the ledger is a read-modify-write on a shared file.

method.repairedThroughOwningBuildScript: Every change is a source change in the owning build script. No generated artifact was hand-edited; every committed output in this diff was produced by rerunning its build script.
method.corpus: scripts/rcap-corpus/bootstrap-private-corpus.sh mounted the pinned Master Library in this container. Archive SHA-256 a26e3ca7d52db4460e53c2eddd893109037702f5c8035f2c698a7e16bad84e89 verified; 51 jurisdictions, 499 files, 329 PDFs; governance checksums verified.

feeWaiverRestraint.whatWasAlmostWritten: A first draft named FW-001 and gave its official title, 'Request to Waive Court Fees'.
feeWaiverRestraint.whyItWasRemoved: That title is not held anywhere in this repository — it was this worker's own knowledge, which is exactly the class of fact the factory forbids. It was cut and the sentence now carries only what the manifest says.
feeWaiverRestraint.secondRestraint: data/rcap-grade-a/launch-control/WAVE_2_VERIFICATION_LEDGER.json records the precise limit of the FW-001 fact: it is California's general fee-waiver form, and that 'does not determine whether either filing has a fee or when a waiver is required.' So the packet NAMES the form — closing the defect — while leaving whether a waiver is available on this petition with the clerk. Naming a form is not the same as establishing an entitlement, and the section says so.

howTheHostChangeWasScoped.problem: The delegating paragraph is shared by all seven California families on this host, and every one of their manifests holds the same file, serve_party and apply_fee_waiver entries. A host-wide fix would have silently rewritten six unclaimed families' participant instructions as a side effect of one repair, and would have made the West control meaningless.
howTheHostChangeWasScoped.solution: A per-family opt-in flag, statesHeldParticipantActions, set on ca-851-91-set alone. The mechanism reads each family's own manifest and is fully general; the other six need only the flag.
howTheHostChangeWasScoped.whyNotHostWide: This worker holds a repair claim on ca-851-91-set and on no other family on this host. Rewriting unclaimed families is not this lane's to do, however correct the rewrite would be.
howTheHostChangeWasScoped.forTheCaptain: The remaining six California families on this host — ca-1203-41-set, ca-1203-42-set, ca-1203-43-set, ca-1203-4a-set, ca-17b-reduction-set and ca-prop64-set — all carry the identical defect and all have manifests that answer it. ca-1203-4a-set additionally holds a REAL fee figure the packet does not state: 'Reimbursement of up to $60 to the county and $60 to the city, subject to an ability-to-pay determination', and ca-prop64-set's pay_fee entry reads 'The source review does not state a filing fee for the CR-400 series.' Each is a one-line flag flip once claimed.

azFamilyDoesNotReproduce.finding: This family's COMMITTED artifacts cannot be reproduced from the committed build script at base 55f3cbeff. Rebuilding it does not reproduce its output — it REGRESSES it, substantially.
whatIsLost: participant-instructions.md collapses from a 69-line hand-written filing-instructions document — with a titled route heading, a 'Where you file this' section naming the Superior Court caption destination, and a fee/service delegation paragraph — down to a 13-line generic 'Participant and reviewer instructions' stub with a bare field list.

azFamilyDoesNotReproduce.causationEstablished: This was NOT caused by this worker's edit, and that was proven rather than asserted. The West host was reverted to its base bytes with git checkout, the AZ family was rebuilt from the pristine base script, and it produced the identical regression. The host was then restored from a copy taken before the test.
azFamilyDoesNotReproduce.whyItMatters: A Grade-A family whose committed artifacts cannot be regenerated from its committed source is not reproducible, and reproducibility is what the whole hash-binding apparatus rests on. Any lane that rebuilds this family for any reason will silently destroy a wave-2 feature and a hand-written participant document. It is a trap laid for the next worker on this host.
azFamilyDoesNotReproduce.likelyCause: Not diagnosed here — out of this lane's grant. The shape of it (committed output is RICHER than the script produces) suggests the committed artifacts were built by a later version of the script than the one on this branch, or that a guidance/config block was lost in a merge.
azFamilyDoesNotReproduce.siblingAtRisk: az_marijuana_expungement_superior_court-set shares this host. It was NOT rebuilt — deliberately, to avoid damaging a second unclaimed family — so whether it shares the condition is unknown and worth checking before anyone rebuilds it.
azFamilyDoesNotReproduce.actionTaken: The AZ family directory was fully reverted with git checkout and is byte-identical to base in this diff. Nothing of this finding is left in the working tree.

forTheCaptain.detail: The brief allowed for the possibility that A2 was wrong about a specific family, and said a disproof would be worth more than a repair. It is not wrong about any of these four. In each case the route obligation census names the record, and the record answers the question. Arkansas, Wisconsin and New York each name their compiled state profile as a requiredSourceId and each profile answers the fee outright; Wisconsin's answer is additionally held a second time in the census row's own destination detail. California names no profile — the manifest is its binding record, which is exactly the question VT8 raised and A2 answered.
